clues: This flat city sits where a river meets the sea in the west of Europe. Rings of still canals cross its streets like slow roads of water.
Frost comes here only when cold winds blow in from the deep mainland. Most nights stay mild, since close sea air and town heat soften the chill.
In 1983 the land's rule book first called this city the capital by that word. New kings still take their oath and crown here.
Rings of canals loop through this city, and bikes rule its streets. Folks pedal past rows of tall thin houses that line each canal.
Kings take their crown in this city, in a church by its royal palace. The government and top court do their daily work in The Hague.
